meta.notes: Media-intro draft. Schema aligned with learning-map-v3. Public exam only: Paper 1 (visual presentation of a theme) requires work in two dimensions; Paper 2 (Design) allows any media/style/technique for design problems—exam-hall presentation is usually flat. SBA has no paper split—3D media are valid for SBA artwork and the process/research workbook. `paper2Applicable: false` means not a typical portable exam-hall 2D Paper 1 submission; for Paper 2 Design follow the brief (usually flat presentation)—not “excluded from SBA”. No real HKEAA papers. No embedded images.
meta.mascot: O2 otter only if mentioned; no other mascots
meta.images: none embedded; prefer no image refs in this draft

units.title: Media intro: Painting (acrylic / oil)
units.intro: Short unit on paint, brushwork, layers and composition. Suitable for exam Paper 1 (2D required), Paper 2 Design presentation (usually flat), and SBA media trials. (Content pending teacher review)
units.paper2Note: Suitable for Paper 1 (2D required) and Paper 2 Design presentation (usually flat). Submit dry, portable 2D pieces.
safetyNotes: Ventilate oil solvents; keep away from flames.
Do not blow-dry paint with your mouth.
Wash hands after; never pour solvent down the sink.

lessons.title: Paints and tools: getting started
cards: Painting builds shape, colour and texture on a flat surface.
Acrylic thins with water and dries fast; oil thins with oil and dries slowly for layering.
Prepare the ground: paper, card or canvas. Dark or light grounds change how colours feel.
Task: paint three small swatches—dots, short strokes, long sweeps—and note which suits which subjects.

quiz.question: What usually thins acrylic paint?
quiz.explain: Acrylic uses water; oil paint uses oil.

quiz.question: Oil paint dries ____, which helps slow layering.

lessons.title: Colour, layers and composition
cards: Thin then thick: keep underlayers thin; thicker paint can sit in front.
Placing complementary colours side by side can make the subject pop.
Empty space (negative space) is part of the composition—you need not fill every gap.
Task: paint a still life with only three colours plus white to practise mixing.

quiz.question: Why paint 'thin then thick'?
quiz.explain: Thin grounds support thicker top layers.

quiz.question: Match medium to trait
quiz.explain: Both are painting media with different drying speeds.

lessons.title: Reading a painting with DAIE
cards: Describe: what shapes, colours and marks do you see? (Hold meaning for later.)
Analyse: which lines or blocks guide the eye? How is depth built?
Interpret: what mood or story might it suggest? Use visual evidence.
Evaluate: which idea will you borrow for Paper 2 / SBA, and why?
Task: write four DAIE sentences about one demo or peer work.

quiz.question: In DAIE, 'Describe' should first…
quiz.explain: Description lists what is visible before judgement.

quiz.question: Evaluation needs visual ____ to support your judgement.

units.title: Media intro: Drawing / sketching
units.intro: Short unit on line, tone, proportion and looking. Common in Paper 1, Paper 2 Design presentation, and the research workbook. (Content pending teacher review)
units.paper2Note: Suitable for Paper 1 (2D required) and Paper 2 Design presentation. Fix charcoal with spray or cover sheets to avoid smudging.
safetyNotes: Spray fixative in a ventilated spot; never toward faces.
Do not blow charcoal dust at classmates.

lessons.title: Line and shape: from seeing to drawing
cards: Drawing records form with line and tone.
Check overall proportion before details; do not start with eyes and mouth.
Light construction lines first; darker lines for edges and shade.
Task: three 2-minute sketches—fix proportion only; do not erase everything and restart.

quiz.question: What should come first when starting?
Quick sketches focus on ____ and big shapes.

lessons.title: Tone and texture
cards: Light direction sets highlight, shade and cast shadow.
Hatching, cross-hatching or blending can build tone without solid fills.
Smooth surfaces reflect more; rough surfaces break the tone into fragments.
Task: draw the same apple twice—hatching once, blending once—and compare texture.

quiz.question: Where do cast shadows usually fall?
options: Near the side away from the light
quiz.answer: Near the side away from the light
quiz.explain: Cast shadows sit on the unlit side.

quiz.question: Match techniques

lessons.title: Drawing in research: DAIE one-liners
cards: Describe: which lines are thickest or densest?
Analyse: how does tone separate front and back?
Interpret: what feeling does this sketch keep?
Evaluate: which proportion or tone will you change next?
Task: paste one sketch in the visual diary with four DAIE lines.

quiz.question: Sketches in the workbook mainly…
quiz.explain: Sketches serve observation and media trials.

quiz.question: DAIE 'Analyse' talks about ____ relationships such as tone and structure.

units.title: Media intro: Sculpture (3D)
units.intro: Short unit on form, mass, space and support. Exam Paper 1 requires 2D work—a 3D object is not a typical portable exam-hall Paper 1 submission. Paper 2 (Design) follows the design brief; presentation is usually flat boards/drawings—do not hand in a large 3D object as the exam-hall piece. SBA has no Paper 1/Paper 2 split, so sculpture is valid for SBA artwork and the process/research workbook. Photos and sketches document the work and can feed a flat Paper 1 or Design presentation. (Content pending teacher review)
units.paper2Note: Exam Paper 1 requires 2D work—a 3D object is not a typical portable exam-hall Paper 1 submission. Paper 2 (Design) follows the design brief; presentation is usually flat boards/drawings—do not hand in a large 3D object as the exam-hall piece. SBA has no Paper 1/Paper 2 split, so sculpture is valid for SBA artwork and the process/research workbook. Photos and sketches document the work and can feed a flat Paper 1 or Design presentation.
safetyNotes: Point sharp tools down; count them in after class.
Heavy pieces need a stable base.
Use a mask and ventilation for dusty materials.

lessons.title: Volume and space: look all round
cards: Sculpture is three-dimensional—view front, back, sides and top.
Mass: big blocks feel heavy; voids or thin posts feel light.
Negative space (holes and gaps) matters as much as solid form.
Task: crumple foil into a 'heavy' form and a 'light' form; turn and compare.

quiz.question: When viewing sculpture you should…
Gaps inside a work are called ____ space.

lessons.title: Structure and safe support
cards: An armature supports long arms or thin necks.
Bases must be wide enough; keep the centre of gravity over the base.
Block out big forms before detail.
Task: sketch an armature for a standing figure and mark weak points.

quiz.question: An armature mainly…
Match ideas

lessons.title: Recording 3D: photo + drawing + DAIE
cards: Photograph against a plain backdrop with a scale marker.
Orthographic sketches (front/side/top) help plan a flat Paper 1 or Design presentation.
Describe the widest face; analyse balance; interpret pose; evaluate the strongest angle.
Task: three photos + four DAIE lines in the workbook for one class sculpture.

quiz.question: Can a 3D sculpture be a typical exam-hall Paper 1 submission?
quiz.explain: Paper 1 requires 2D; Paper 2 Design follows the brief (usually flat). SBA has no paper split—3D OK for SBA.

quiz.question: Record 3D trials with ____ and sketches in the workbook.
wordBank: the real 3D object as the paper

units.title: Media intro: Printmaking
units.intro: Short unit on relief/intaglio ideas, transfer and editions. Suitable for Paper 1 (2D required) and Paper 2 Design presentation. (Content pending teacher review)
units.paper2Note: Prints are flat and suit Paper 1 and Paper 2 Design presentation. Follow teacher rules for knives and ink.
safetyNotes: Cut away from your body; keep the other hand behind the blade path.
Use gloves/apron; dispose of solvents safely.

lessons.title: How a print is made
cards: Printmaking builds an image on a plate, then transfers it to paper under pressure.
Relief: ink sits on raised areas. Intaglio: ink sits in recesses.
One plate can make many impressions.
Task: carve a simple stamp (eraser/potato) and pull three prints comparing pressure.

quiz.question: Where does relief ink mainly sit?
Multiple pulls from one plate are called ____.

lessons.title: Design and transfer tips
cards: Text on the plate prints mirrored—plan a reverse design.
Even ink: too thick smudges; too thin breaks lines.
Cleaning and re-cutting are valid trials—photograph them for the workbook.
Task: design a symbol—draw the forward sketch, then the mirrored plate plan.

quiz.question: Text on a plate will print…
Match ink problems

lessons.title: DAIE: reading a print
cards: Describe cut marks versus roller traces.
Analyse how black/white contrast makes rhythm.
Interpret whether repeats strengthen or change meaning.
Evaluate which impression is final and why.
Task: compare best and weakest pulls with DAIE.

quiz.question: Best workbook evidence for print trials is…
DAIE 'Interpret' links the image to possible ____.

units.title: Media intro: Fashion design
units.intro: Short unit from theme and silhouette to materials and flats. Flat fashion drawings / boards suit Paper 1 (2D required) and Paper 2 (Design) presentation. Constructed garments are not typical portable exam-hall pieces (follow the brief; usually flat); they may be used in SBA if the school’s SBA brief allows 3D. (Content pending teacher review)
units.paper2Note: Flat fashion drawings / boards suit Paper 1 (2D required) and Paper 2 (Design) presentation. Constructed garments are not typical portable exam-hall pieces (follow the brief; usually flat); they may be used in SBA if the school’s SBA brief allows 3D.
safetyNotes: Pass scissors closed.
Store pins in a box—never leave them on desks.

lessons.title: Theme and silhouette
cards: Decide wearer and occasion before silhouette.
Silhouette is the outer outline from afar: A-line, straight, fitted, etc.
Mood boards gather colour and texture; do not copy finished-garment photos as answers.
Task: three silhouette thumbnails for 'rainy school day'.

quiz.question: Silhouette mainly means…
An inspiration image board is a ____ board.

lessons.title: Materials and flat illustrations
cards: The same silhouette feels different in denim vs chiffon.
Flats need body proportion plus material and detail call-outs.
Swatch tests beside the drawing count as media experiments.
Task: one flat + two annotated swatches (absorbency / drape).

quiz.question: What suits the exam hall better?
options: A live model on the spot
quiz.explain: Paper 1 requires 2D; Paper 2 Design is usually flat presentation. Garments may suit SBA if the school brief allows 3D.

quiz.question: Match

lessons.title: DAIE: reviewing a design board
cards: Describe colours, lines and accessories.
Analyse how silhouette fits the occasion.
Interpret identity or mood suggested.
Evaluate which detail best strengthens the theme.
Task: peer DAIE on a classmate's board—stay respectful.

quiz.question: In peer review you should…
Evaluation should offer workable ____ suggestions.

units.title: Media intro: Paper sculpture
units.intro: Short unit on folding, cutting, layering and support. Exam Paper 1 requires 2D—paper sculpture is not a typical portable exam-hall Paper 1 submission. Paper 2 (Design) follows the brief; presentation is usually flat—do not hand in large paper sculpture as the exam-hall piece. SBA has no paper split, so paper sculpture is valid for SBA artwork and the process/research workbook; record with nets/photos, which can also feed a flat Paper 1 or Design presentation. (Content pending teacher review)
units.paper2Note: Exam Paper 1 requires 2D—paper sculpture is not a typical portable exam-hall Paper 1 submission. Paper 2 (Design) follows the brief; presentation is usually flat—do not hand in large paper sculpture as the exam-hall piece. SBA has no paper split, so paper sculpture is valid for SBA artwork and the process/research workbook; record with nets/photos, which can also feed a flat Paper 1 or Design presentation.
safetyNotes: Use knife with ruler and mat; fingers clear of the blade.
Clear scraps to prevent slips.

lessons.title: Paper can become 3D
cards: Creases make edges; cuts open space.
Layered card can feel like relief (still semi-3D).
Grain direction affects strength.
Task: one A4 sheet—only three cuts and five folds—must stand on the table.

quiz.question: What most often makes paper stand?
Layered work stuck to a backboard gives a ____ effect.

lessons.title: Structure: slots and glue
cards: Slot joints need less glue and rebuild easily.
Thin glue; thick glue wrinkles paper.
Hide supports inside (triangle folds or inner posts).
Task: a slot-joint animal head with no glue.

quiz.question: A benefit of slot joints is…
Match

lessons.title: Recording and DAIE
cards: Photo front/side/top; also draw a net.
Describe layers; analyse supports; interpret theme; evaluate stability.
For Paper 1 or Design presentation, turn nets or tonal drawings into flat work.
Task: one net + four stability DAIE lines.

quiz.question: Can paper sculpture be a typical exam-hall Paper 1 piece?
quiz.explain: Paper 1 requires 2D; Paper 2 Design follows the brief (usually flat). SBA has no paper split—3D OK for SBA.

quiz.question: A flat pattern that folds into 3D is often called a ____.

units.title: Media intro: Clay / ceramic clay (陶泥)
units.intro: Short unit on clay / ceramic clay (陶泥): wedging, joining, moisture and surface. Exam Paper 1 requires 2D—a clay / ceramic-clay (陶泥) object is not a typical portable exam-hall Paper 1 submission. Paper 2 (Design) follows the brief; presentation is usually flat—do not hand in a large clay or ceramic piece as the exam-hall work. SBA has no paper split, so clay / ceramic clay is valid for SBA artwork and the process/research workbook; record with photos, sections and texture rubbings, which can also feed a flat Paper 1 or Design presentation. (Content pending teacher review)
units.paper2Note: Exam Paper 1 requires 2D—a clay / ceramic-clay (陶泥) object is not a typical portable exam-hall Paper 1 submission. Paper 2 (Design) follows the brief; presentation is usually flat—do not hand in a large clay or ceramic piece as the exam-hall work. SBA has no paper split, so clay / ceramic clay is valid for SBA artwork and the process/research workbook; record with photos, sections and texture rubbings, which can also feed a flat Paper 1 or Design presentation.
materials: Clay / ceramic clay 陶泥 (as assigned)
safetyNotes: Wipe clay dust damp—do not dry-sweep; mask if needed.
Do not wash large clay scraps down the sink.
Only teachers fire the kiln.

lessons.title: Clay basics: wedge and air
cards: Wedging removes air pockets that cause cracks or kiln blow-ups.
Too dry cracks; too wet collapses—control with spray and bags.
Solid blocks or coils both work if joins are strong.
Task: ten even coils into a small cup form—stable over pretty.

quiz.question: Wedging mainly…
Clay that is too dry tends to ____.

lessons.title: Joins and texture
cards: Score and slip before joining.
Stamps, fabric and carving create texture trials.
Keep wall thickness even for even drying.
Task: two texture tiles with tool labels.

quiz.question: Score and slip means…
Match

lessons.title: Recording clay + DAIE
cards: Photo wedge, join, texture and finish.
Texture rubbings on paper can feed flat Paper 1 or Design presentation work.
Describe thickness; analyse joins; interpret form; evaluate next changes.
Task: four process photos + four DAIE lines.

quiz.question: Can a clay object be a typical exam-hall Paper 1 piece?
quiz.explain: Paper 1 requires 2D; Paper 2 Design follows the brief (usually flat). SBA has no paper split—3D OK for SBA.

quiz.question: Before joining, ____ the contact faces, then add slip.

units.title: Media intro: Collage
units.intro: Short unit on layering, cutting/tearing, contrast and composition. Suitable for Paper 1 (2D required) and Paper 2 Design presentation. Use only self-made, cleared or teacher-provided materials. (Content pending teacher review)
units.paper2Note: Flat collage suits Paper 1 and Paper 2 Design presentation. Avoid uncleared magazine photos; prefer your photos, text-only newsprint, coloured paper.
safetyNotes: Wipe glue spills at once.
Pass scissors closed.

lessons.title: Collage = choose and juxtapose
cards: Collage cuts and sticks materials into a new image.
Material history and texture are part of the content.
Torn edges feel softer; cut edges feel sharper.
Task: one small composition from only three pieces.

quiz.question: The core of collage is…
Torn edges usually feel more ____ than cut edges.

lessons.title: Layers, space and copyright
cards: Large pieces ground the design; small pieces make focal points.
Empty space lets the work breathe.
Do not submit uncleared celebrity photos or copyrighted illustrations.
Task: list the source of every piece you used.

quiz.question: For exam-hall flat collage you should…
Match

lessons.title: DAIE: reading a collage
cards: Describe materials and edge types.
Analyse how overlap builds depth.
Interpret new meanings from juxtaposition.
Evaluate the strongest contrast.
Task: DAIE on your work; change only one variable next.

quiz.question: Interpretation in collage especially watches…
Next trial should change ____ main variable at a time.

units.title: Media intro: Colour pencil / pastel
units.intro: Short unit on dry-media layering, mixing and surface care. Suitable for Paper 1 (2D required) and Paper 2 Design presentation. (Content pending teacher review)
units.paper2Note: Dry-media flat work suits Paper 1 and Paper 2 Design presentation. Fix or cover pastels.
safetyNotes: Spray fixative with ventilation.
Do not blow pastel dust at people; wash hands.

lessons.title: Colour pencil: layers and direction
cards: Mix by layering, usually light to dark.
Stroke direction can follow form for volume.
Reserve highlights; do not fill everything at once.
Task: one sphere with two stroke-direction approaches.

quiz.question: Colour-pencil mixing mainly uses…
Strokes can follow the ____ of the form.

lessons.title: Pastel: body and blend
cards: Pastel is powdery; blend lightly with care for hygiene.
Dark grounds make pastels glow; light grounds control layers.
Fix or cover finished work.
Task: gradients on dark and light grounds.

quiz.question: Before handing in pastel work…
options: Fix or add a cover sheet
quiz.answer: Fix or add a cover sheet

quiz.question: Match

lessons.title: DAIE: dry-media surfaces
cards: Describe strokes versus powder.
Analyse layer order.
Interpret how texture fits mood.
Evaluate which dry medium fits your exam / SBA topic.
Task: same subject, both media; DAIE compare.

quiz.question: When comparing dry media, best practice is…
options: Same subject, change only the medium
quiz.answer: Same subject, change only the medium

quiz.question: Do not ____ pastel dust toward classmates.

units.title: Media intro: Watercolour
units.intro: Short unit on water control, transparent layers and reserved whites. Suitable for Paper 1 (2D required) and Paper 2 Design presentation. (Content pending teacher review)
units.paper2Note: Flat watercolour suits Paper 1 and Paper 2 Design presentation. Fully dry before submission; use interleaving sheets.
safetyNotes: Paints are usually low-toxicity but not for eating.
Do not splash rinse water at people.

lessons.title: Water-to-paint ratio
cards: Water carries pigment: more water = lighter; less = stronger.
Wet-on-wet: damp paper lets colour bloom.
Wet-on-dry: sharper edges on dry paper.
Task: five swatches of one colour from strong to pale.

quiz.question: Wet-on-wet often gives…
More water usually makes colour more ____.

lessons.title: Glazing and reserved whites
cards: Watercolour is mostly transparent—underlayers show through.
Highlights are often reserved paper white.
Let a layer dry before the next to avoid lifting.
Task: a simple glass with reserved highlights.

quiz.question: A common way to make highlights is…
Match

lessons.title: DAIE: reading watercolour layers
cards: Describe lightest and darkest areas.
Analyse new colours from transparent overlays.
Interpret how water traces become mood.
Evaluate your best water control; plan one change.
Task: photo the dry work with DAIE and wet/dry labels.

quiz.question: Before another glaze you should…
Watercolours for the exam hall must be fully ____.

units.title: Media intro: Ink / ink wash
units.intro: Short unit on value, brush methods, line and wash. Suitable for Paper 1 (2D required) and Paper 2 Design presentation; may connect to Chinese painting traditions without copying famous works as submissions. (Content pending teacher review)
units.paper2Note: Flat ink work suits Paper 1 and Paper 2 Design presentation. Dry xuan paper fully and protect from tearing.
safetyNotes: Do not drink ink; wear an apron.
Dispose of rinse water properly.

lessons.title: Value and water
cards: Ink can move through dark-to-light steps (use a classroom-simplified scale).
Water in the brush changes wetness and flying-white textures.
Test on scrap before the final sheet.
Task: one stroke graded across five boxes dark to light.

quiz.question: Before the final sheet you should…
options: Blow ink away with a dryer

quiz.question: A dry brush with little ink often shows ____ (white threads in the stroke).

lessons.title: Line, dots and wash
cards: Centre-brush lines feel rounder; side-brush lines feel flatter and wider.
Washes can suggest mist or distant hills.
Inscriptions and seals are optional classroom extras.
Task: bamboo leaves with centre-brush vs side-brush.

quiz.question: Side-brush lines usually feel…
Match

lessons.title: DAIE: reading an ink study
cards: Describe darkest lines and flying white.
Analyse how value separates space.
Interpret how empty paper breathes.
Evaluate the strongest stroke to borrow for your theme.
Task: DAIE on your study; AI feedback stays 18+ paid flow—teachers lead in class.

quiz.question: Empty paper in ink work often…
options: Lets the image breathe and imply space
quiz.answer: Lets the image breathe and imply space

quiz.question: Exam Paper 1 ink pieces must be ____ works (not 3D installs).

units.title: Media intro: Technical pen (針筆)
units.intro: Short unit on technical / fineliner / rapidograph-style pens: line weight, hatching and stippling. Dry flat medium—suitable for Paper 1 (2D required) and Paper 2 Design presentation. (Content pending teacher review)
units.paper2Note: Flat technical-pen work suits Paper 1 and Paper 2 Design presentation. Protect line drawings from scratches and moisture.
safetyNotes: Fine nibs—cap when passing; never point at people.
Ink is not for eating; blot clothing stains promptly.
Recap after use to avoid clogging.

lessons.title: Nib size and steady stroke
cards: Steady speed and angle make even lines; stopping mid-stroke leaves blobs.
Light pencil underdrawing first; ink when ready; erase pencil only when dry.
Learn labelled nib widths before forcing variety with pressure alone.
Task: ten parallel lines with each of three nib sizes; compare evenness.

quiz.question: Technical-pen work usually starts with…
After use, ____ the pen to stop clogging.

lessons.title: Hatching, cross-hatching, stippling
cards: Hatching builds tone with parallel lines; cross-hatching darkens.
Stippling uses dot density for smooth value changes.
Reserve whites; build light to dark.
Task: one circle—hatching on the left, stippling on the right.

quiz.question: Stippling mainly controls tone by…
Match

lessons.title: DAIE: reading a pen drawing
cards: Describe: where are lines densest or thickest?
Analyse: how does hatch direction follow form?
Interpret: what mood do clean fine lines suggest?
Evaluate: which technique fits your Paper 1 / Design / SBA topic?
Task: finish a small inked study, write four DAIE lines; add a cover sheet.

quiz.question: For exam Paper 1, technical-pen work must be…
Before submitting pen drawings, add a ____ to avoid scratches.

units.title: Media intro: Photography
units.intro: Short unit on composition, light, selection and flat presentation. Public exams usually submit prints or flat presentation boards—not cameras. Suitable for Paper 1 (2D required) and Paper 2 Design presentation; SBA may also use photographic work and process records. (Content pending teacher review)
units.paper2Note: Photo prints / flat presentation boards suit Paper 1 and Paper 2 Design presentation. Exam hall usually takes flat work, not camera bodies. SBA may include photographic pieces and contact/selection records.
materials: Scissors / craft knife and glue (with teacher)
safetyNotes: Do not photograph people without consent (especially classmates’ faces).
Do not submit unlicensed / infringing found images as your own work.
Follow school phone / camera policy; do not disrupt other classes.
Pass craft knives closed; cut only on a mat.

lessons.title: Composition and light
cards: Photography is choosing what enters the frame and what is cut away.
Rule of thirds, contrast and leading lines are starting points—not the only answers.
Light direction changes mood: front light flattens; side light models; backlight silhouettes.
Task: three shots of one object—front, side and back light—with time and place notes.

quiz.question: Side light usually makes forms…
Exams usually take photo ____ or flat boards, not the camera body.

lessons.title: Selection, series and flat presentation
cards: Shooting more is not enough—select a set that serves the theme.
Contact sheets / thumbnail walls help compare composition and light before final prints.
Presentation: consistent size, margins, title and short caption for readers.
Task: from nine thumbnails pick three as a mini-series; write one theme sentence.

quiz.question: When selecting photos, the priority is…
Match

lessons.title: DAIE + ethics
cards: Describe subject, foreground, background and light direction.
Analyse how composition guides the eye.
Interpret the relationship or mood claimed.
Evaluate which frame best states the theme; plan the next change.
Ethics: consent for portraits; credit sources; do not pass off found images as yours.
Task: four DAIE lines on the final print + one consent / copyright self-check line.

quiz.question: Before photographing a classmate’s face you should…
Do not submit online images without ____ as if they were your original work.
